findings.issue: The inventory has four Astenia entries. None of the ten Astenia stories keys the one under APARELHO HEMOLINFOPOIÉTICO (p.8): “Astenia: Cansaço e fraqueza secundários a quadros como anemias severas.”. All ten carry the same self-check: “A entrada hemolinfopoiética exige vínculo secundário a condição não documentada; não se presume anemia para crédito integral ou parcial.” That is a possible reading, but it is the generator's. Against it: (a) the inventory's caution on this very entry reads “Associações e exemplos de doenças no original não são critérios diagnósticos”; (b) the base stories give full credit to same-label endocrine entries whose description carries a disease association, without any evidence of that disease (Palpitações, “Sensação subjetiva dos batimentos cardíacos (frequente no hipertireoidismo).”; Rouquidão, “Alteração no timbre da voz (disfonia), comum em bócio volumoso ou hipotireoidismo grave.”); (c) in the base, the only same-label entry left out of a key is excluded for body site (APARELHO GENITAL FEMININO > Prurido), never for cause; (d) the batch itself keys the endocrine Astenia “sem doença endócrina presumida”. For it: here the cause sits in the main clause (“secundários a”), not in a parenthesis or a “comum em”. In the game the student chooses term and group; a student who answers Astenia and picks APARELHO HEMOLINFOPOIÉTICO would lose points, although nothing in any of the ten utterances points to the heart either.

findings.resolution: None is supported. Every utterance places the weakness in the whole body or in no body part; 182 and 186 deny a focal deficit in so many words (“não só numa perna”, “Não é um braço que perdeu força”). At 181 (passing a spoon from hand to hand) and 187 (holding a mug) the example task involves the hands; it is framed as effort and exhaustion, and the reading depends on “corpo inteiro”/“corpo todo” in the first sentence. No utterance reports breathlessness, sleepiness, low mood, loss of interest or near-fainting; 183 states preserved will (“Eu quero fazer as coisas”).

findings.issue: Checked for leftovers from another symptom group: none. No Astenia rationale mentions itching or any symptom absent from its utterance, and gendered words agree with the utterances. Three weaker points. (1) Each story rationale is reused verbatim as the evidence rationale of the cardiovascular path, and at indices 181, 182, 184, 185, 187 and 189 that text argues only for the other path (“sustenta também a entrada endocrinológica”, “sustenta também Fadiga”), so the cardiovascular evidence entry carries no reasoning of its own. (2) The other evidence rationales are one stock sentence per entry (“A fala documenta os critérios da entrada …”) followed by the description; at index 184 that sentence asserts a persistence the utterance does not state (B027-03). (3) The rationale of index 180 uses the endocrine entry's wording (“generalizada”, “sem esforço proporcional”) while leaving that entry out (B027-02).
findings.resolution: Not a reason to hold by itself. Since the app shows the rationale to the student, the cardiovascular evidence entry should say why the cardiovascular description is met.

findings.resolution: Passed. Swelling of feet, ankles or lower legs with a dent after pressure is, to the reviewer's general knowledge, the ordinary bedside picture of oedema, and the five descriptions give no ground for choosing one block over another. Teaching confirmation recommended on two points: that the five blocks always score together, and that a swelling described without the pitting sign would also be accepted (the stories never test that).

findings.issue: Seven utterances use the source's own word (“inchados”, “inchadas”, “inchaço”, “inchada”: indices 190, 192, 193, 195, 196, 198, 199), which makes them easy; 191, 194 and 197 describe the swelling without naming it. Index 191 says only that the skin “fica marcada por um tempo”, less precise than a dent. Index 196 denies a lump (“não é um caroço isolado”) in a slightly leading way. Index 199 reports a demonstration (“Mostrei como o dedo deixa um buraco…”) without saying to whom. All ten are the same picture (lower limbs, pitting): no story places the swelling elsewhere.
